title: Observation-only on incumbent f6d4b8d3: terminal saturation by GetUserTweets is a workload-composition fact and the wal_wait alert is refuted by combined wal_timing + wait-event + host_io evidence; no concurrency/maintenance knob group is justified

anomaly.aggregation: class total latency seconds / (terminals * measured duration) = 848.42s / 960s

configuration_cause: No knob in incumbent f6d4b8d367c7e40328ecd942458760992e37f410fb160b630ec667b47d69427c is implicated in the dominant anomaly. Lock/connection/concurrency evidence is flat: locks_waiting median/p95/max = 0/0/0, lock_waiting_backends max 0, deadlocks 0/s, conflicts 0/s, numbackends max 9 against max_connections 137. Maintenance evidence is quiescent: n_dead_tup 0.08/s, autovacuum_count 0.0248/s, autoanalyze_count 0.0186/s, checkpoints_req 0.0/s, buffers_checkpoint 6.56/s, temp_files 0/s. The secondary high-severity alert 'wal_wait' is a single instantaneous sample (wal_waiting_backends median 0.0 / p95 0.0 / max 1 out of 9 backends, 148 samples) and is refuted by the combined write-path evidence: wal_timing.write_average_ms = 0.1379, wal_sync 0/s, wal_sync_time_per_txn 0.0, wal_write_time_per_txn 0.00104 ms, and host_io some/full stall fraction 0.0 with zero io_pressure_some/full time. Low WAL volume (146 KB/s, 5.17 B/txn) is not the basis of this conclusion; the timing and stall counters are.
mechanism: Closed-loop terminal budget: TPS = terminals / weighted mean client latency. GetUserTweets is 3,048,834 of 3,441,196 client transactions (88.6% of calls) and consumes 848.42s of the 8 x 120s = 960s terminal budget (0.884) at a 169us median / 278us mean. Its cost is a shared-memory index probe: buffer_hit_ratio 0.99993, blks_read 20.1/s, blk_read_time 0.203 ms/s, idx_scan 21,945/s, seq_scan 0/s, temp_bytes 0. The tail is a rare per-call micro-stall (GetUserTweets p99 2813us, but GetTweetsFromFollowing max 32,155us with fraction 0.0386), not a queue: lock_waiting_backends and locks_waiting are identically zero, so no wait queue exists for any lock, connection, vacuum or WAL knob to drain. The 'waiting_backends' gauge (median 2 / p95 7 / max 7) decomposes into client_waiting_backends (max 5, i.e. closed-loop client idle, consistent with idle_in_transaction max 5) plus io_waiting_backends max 1 plus wal_waiting_backends max 1; it is not lock or WAL backpressure. Therefore the smallest coherent knob group supported by evidence is the empty group.

intermediate_metrics.source: pg_stat_wal + track_wal_io_timing / track_io_timing (diagnostic_instrumentation changed to on)

query_effect: None. No plan, executor path, I/O path, lock mode or durability path is altered; knob_changes is empty.
expected_tps_effect: Unchanged: next measurement is expected inside the verified replicate band 29,762.6-31,906.7 rps (median 30,213.6), allowing for the wider observed run-to-run span 28,257.5-31,906.7 across the four runs of this config.
expected_latency_effect: Unchanged: overall p95 ~646-754us, overall p99 ~2349-2899us, GetUserTweets p50 ~157-169us and p99 ~2280-2813us.

predictions.rationale: No knob changes, so the closed-loop identity TPS = 8 terminals / mean client latency is untouched. Verified replicates span 29,762.6-31,906.7 rps (median 30,213.6) and the four observed runs of this same config span 28,257.5-31,906.7 rps (12.7% span), so a no-op prediction is stated as unchanged within 8%.

0.8838 = 848.42s of 960s; baseline runs gave 0.8798/0.8817/0.8787 (spread 0.3pp). With zero knob changes neither the call count (~3.05M of 3.44M) nor the mean latency (278us on cached index probes) can move, so the fraction stays within 3pp of 0.884.
WAL write average is 0.1379 ms with wal_sync 0/s and host_io some/full stall fraction 0.0; there is no WAL write queue, so no commit/WAL knob can move the mean write service time by 25% (0.034 ms).

The wal_wait alarm rests on one instantaneous sample: median 0.0, p95 0.0, max 1 of ~9 backends over 148 samples, against 0.0072 WAL writes per transaction. Reconfiguring the commit/WAL pipeline cannot remove a wait that is already at the noise floor, so the max should not rise by 1 or more backends.

locks_waiting median/p95/max = 0/0/0, lock_waiting_backends max 0, deadlocks 0/s and conflicts 0/s; with no knob change and 8 terminals there is no lock conflict to create or relieve, so this stays at 0 backends.

Dead-tuple generation is 0.08/s and autovacuum_count is 0.0248/s against autovacuum_vacuum_scale_factor 0.128 on a cache-resident read-mostly snapshot; holding the incumbent autovacuum knobs leaves that background rate within 25% of 0.0248/s over a 120s window.

idle_in_transaction median 0 / p95 3 / max 5 alongside client_waiting_backends max 5 shows the waiting gauge is closed-loop client idle, not a database wait. No concurrency/maintenance knob governs client think time, so the max stays within 1 backend of 5.

alternatives.statement: The wal_wait alert is a genuine WAL write/fsync stall that one instantaneous observation under-resolves, so a WAL/commit-path knob (e.g. wal_sync_method, wal_writer_delay/wal_writer_flush_after, commit_delay/commit_siblings) would help.

The GetUserTweets p99 (2813us, vs 169us median) is caused by lock-manager or buffer-LWLock contention among the 8 concurrent terminals on hot index pages, which the terminal_capacity_fraction framing hides.

The replicate-to-replicate throughput spread (28,257.5 vs 31,906.7 rps) is produced by autovacuum/checkpoint background writeback stealing CPU/IO from the read path, which vacuum/checkpoint knobs would fix.

cross_domain_requirements: query_execution: EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) plus wait_event sampling on the exact GetUserTweets SQL to attribute its 2813us p99 tail (executor vs LWLock vs client idle).
memory_storage: confirm the WAL/commit path needs no change; this proposal refutes a slow-fsync cause via wal_timing, wait events and host_io together.
why_exceeds_incumbent: It does not exceed the incumbent; it refuses an unjustified change and protects a verified-healthy configuration. Acting on the single-sample wal_wait alert would perturb a write path that costs 0.0072 WAL writes and 0.00104 ms of WAL write time per transaction, and acting on vacuum knobs where dead tuples accrue at 0.08/s has no mechanism. The only evidence-supported action is to hold the incumbent and confirm the frozen no-change predictions; an intervention here would add restart/reload risk and measurement cost for a predicted null effect.
